Each processor can execute one instruction every 500500 nanoseconds as long as memory references are satisfied by its local cache. When a cache miss occurs, the processor is delayed for an additional 2,0002,000 nanoseconds. During half of this additional delay, the bus is dedicated to serving the cache miss. During the other half, the processor cannot continue, but the bus is free to service requests from other processors. On average, each instruction requires 22 memory references. What proportion of the capacity of the bus would a single processor consume, ignoring delays due to competition from other processors?
